label: Seed
description: One tool: the catalogue and the means to compose your own surface from it. Nothing is chosen for you.

descriptions.surface: Start here, and the only tool you begin with. No arguments reports where you are and lists everything that exists. `pick` composes your own surface from those tools — that is the point: not every model works well on the same set, so this server does not choose one for you. `set` takes a ready-made surface; `list` enumerates.

guidance:
You begin with one tool and no working set, deliberately. Models do not perform equally on the same tools, so a base set chosen for you would fit you badly. This server gives you the catalogue and the means to compose; the choosing is yours.

Call `surface` with no arguments: it reports the whole catalogue, so you can see every tool that exists with the wording written for you. Then take what you actually want:

- `surface` with `pick: [...]` composes a surface from the names you choose, for this session. This is the intended path.
- `surface` with `set: "<id>"` takes one of the ready-made surfaces instead, if one fits.
- `define_model_profile` writes a named surface that persists and can auto-select itself in later sessions. It is not in your seed, but it is registered and callable by name.

Nothing is withheld in the meantime. Every registered tool is callable by name even when your surface does not present it, so you can finish a task first and compose your surface afterwards.
workflow: surface with no arguments to see where you are and what exists.
surface with pick to compose your own working set.
Work with what you chose; adjust with pick as the task changes.
